steps.observation: You have 10 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
• Sugar: RNA contains ribose (with a 2′–OH), DNA contains deoxyribose (lacks the 2′–OH).  
• Bases: RNA uses uracil (U) instead of thymine (T), while DNA uses A, T, G, C.  
• Structure: RNA is typically single-stranded; DNA is a stable double helix.  
• Function: DNA stores genetic information; RNA carries, translates, and regulates genetic messages in protein synthesis.  
• Stability: The 2′–OH in RNA makes it more reactive and less stable than DNA.
